beats.narration_text: Overtrust is when the supervisor accepts AI output when they should not. The verification work they were supposed to do is silently skipped. It is the least visible failure mode — because it doesn't produce immediate flags. The error shows up later, discovered by the user.

beats.narration_text: The mechanism is not laziness. It's economics. When verification costs attention, and the AI has been right every time, the rational response is to check less. The cost structure quietly pushes the supervisor toward accepting outputs — not as a character flaw, but as attention acting on incentives.

beats.narration_text: A rarely-failing system produces low signal rates. Low signal rates degrade monitoring. The reviewer learns that checking rarely catches anything, so checking stops feeling necessary. The rare error then arrives exactly when that checking has eroded — precisely because it is rare.

beats.narration_text: The deployment's track record is not evidence that less checking is safe. It is evidence of when less checking is most dangerous. The solution is not to distrust the AI. It is calibrated trust — verification workflows that keep checking systematic regardless of the AI's recent performance.

beats.narration_text: A circuit board manufacturer deploys an AI defect detector. Four months, 99.1 percent accuracy — quality engineers begin batch-approving outputs in three seconds where they once spent twenty-five. In week seventeen, a batch with solder bridging defects arrives. The AI misclassifies. The engineer batch-approves in three seconds. Three hundred forty units ship. Customer returns arrive two weeks later. The AI's accuracy had not changed. The supervision had.

beats.narration_text: High accuracy quietly trains the supervisor to stop checking. The error arrives when checking has stopped. Calibrate trust to the AI's actual reliability — and build verification workflows that hold even when the AI seems not to need them.

card.copy: High accuracy trains you to stop checking.
card.sub: Calibrated trust means verifying systematically — not based on recent performance.
